title: Success is Hard Until You Understand This Formula
promo_conflict: Codie promotes her own Growth Boardroom, book, free event and advisory services; the Boardroom and media returns are self-reported.

stated_problem.quote: A business owner who wants to make more profit with less pain.
stated_problem.speaker: Codie Sanchez

idea.name: Growth Boardroom owner coaching
idea.one_liner: Coaching and growth planning for established business owners, sold through an annual membership with advisory and exit-preparation tiers.
idea.customer: Established business owners looking to grow or prepare to sell.
idea.offer: Boardroom advisors coach owners through custom growth plans; higher-touch help prepares businesses for sale.
idea.revenue_model: $24K per year to join; the transcript also describes a free event and an exit-ready advisory tier, whose prices are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: For our growth boardroom, we charge 24K a year to join.
It's targeted at established owners looking to grow.
the average boardroom member grows by 130K a year when they pay us 24K a year?
Boardroom is where our advisors personally coach you through a custom growth plan and resources to move faster than they ever could alone.

claims.claim: The Boardroom membership costs 24K per year.
claims.quote: For our growth boardroom, we charge 24K a year to join.

claims.claim: The speaker says the average Boardroom member grows by 130K per year while paying 24K per year.
claims.quote: the average boardroom member grows by 130K a year when they pay us 24K a year?

claims.claim: The speaker uses $100,000 and $500,000 as comparison prices for McKinsey or Bain.
claims.quote: Well, I could go out and compete and say, well, actually, this is really low priced versus $100,000 or $500,000 that McKinsey or Bain would charge you.

claims.claim: The speaker frames $106,000 as the value an owner might miss by rejecting the offer.
claims.quote: Well, that's interesting because basically that means that the $24,000 every time they tell me $24,000 is expensive, I say, well, show me that math because instead, we could actually just be saying that it would be really expensive to mix $106,000.

claims.claim: The free event is promoted with a million dollars in cash and prizes.
claims.quote: I give away a million dollars in cash and prizes live.

claims.claim: The advisors are said to have helped thousands of business owners.
claims.quote: If you want to talk to one of my advisors who have helped thousands of business owners with their sales, click the link right here.

acquisition_channels.details: The video promotes the free event and links viewers to a conversation with an advisor.
A free live event and book are described as entry-level offers in the funnel.

ideas.delivery: Advisors personally coach members through custom growth plans; the top tier offers hands-on help to de-risk a business before sale.

prices: Million dollars in event cash and prizes

stated_problem.quote: And he shows up when a pipe bursts in your kitchen at 10 p.m.
stated_problem.speaker: Codie Sanchez

idea.name: Emergency residential plumbing with a priority plan
idea.one_liner: Emergency repairs and plumbing add-ons for homeowners, earning repair fees and recurring revenue from a $10/month priority tier.
idea.customer: Homeowners with urgent leaks or other plumbing problems.
idea.offer: Repair leaks, inspect for related problems and offer priority service for subscribers.
idea.revenue_model: One-off repair charges and a $10/month premium subscription; the transcript presents these as an illustrative scenario.

key_quotes.quote: And he shows up when a pipe bursts in your kitchen at 10 p.m.
If we were actually able to make a case that 15k is what that would have cost you, he could have charged you 1500 bucks.
It's actually just 10 bucks a month to add on top of it.

claims.claim: The illustrative repair takes 20 minutes.
claims.quote: He's there 20 minutes. He tightens one thing.

claims.claim: The illustrative repair bill is 400 bucks.
claims.quote: He stops the leak and he hands you a bill for 400 bucks.

claims.claim: A mold-related gut job could cost $150,000.
claims.quote: That was a gut job. It's $150,000.

claims.claim: The floor at risk of damage is described as worth 5k.
claims.quote: That's pretty nice floor. That looks like 5k.

claims.claim: The water bill could be a couple of hundred bucks.
claims.quote: This could be a couple of hundred bucks just in water in the state of Texas.

claims.claim: If the plumber demonstrates a 15k avoided cost, the example says he could charge 1500 bucks.
claims.quote: If we were actually able to make a case that 15k is what that would have cost you, he could have charged you 1500 bucks.

claims.claim: The customer would be said to have saved $15,000 after the repair.
claims.quote: And you'd still shake his hand and say thanks. He just saved you $15,000.

claims.claim: The plumber is also described as charging 400 for work taking about 10 minutes, differing from the earlier 20-minute description.
claims.quote: He's underpriced at 400. Even though that was like 10 minutes of his time.

claims.claim: An additional plumbing inspection is offered as a 10-minute check.
claims.quote: If your plumbing is wrong here, you want me to take a look at it another 10 minutes.

claims.claim: The premium tier promises priority service within three hours of a problem.
claims.quote: Sometimes I can't because I actually have this level of service where we guarantee somebody within three hours of a problem, they always get first priority.

claims.claim: The priority subscription costs 10 bucks a month.
claims.quote: It's actually just 10 bucks a month to add on top of it.

ideas.delivery: A plumber visits the homeowner to repair leaks, can check for other plumbing problems and can offer the homeowner a recurring priority-service tier.

prices: A couple of hundred bucks (water bill)

ideas.other_uk_rules: The recurring consumer priority tier would need clear terms, cancellation information and compliant subscription handling under applicable UK consumer and DMCC Act rules.

stated_problem.quote: It looks like this HVAC's real old.
stated_problem.speaker: Codie Sanchez

idea.name: Plumber-referred HVAC service
idea.one_liner: HVAC inspections and follow-on work for homeowners referred by plumbers; the transcript also describes an unspecified referral fee paid to the plumber.
idea.customer: Homeowners whose HVAC system may need inspection or service.
idea.offer: A plumber connects a homeowner with an HVAC partner to inspect an aging system.
idea.revenue_model: The HVAC provider earns revenue from service work; the referring plumber receives an unspecified referral fee.

key_quotes.quote: I have a partner that actually helps the HVAC system, which was one of the reasons your pipe burst.
You want me to get them to come out and look at it tomorrow.
He's going to give me a referral fee.

acquisition_channels.details: A plumber refers an existing homeowner customer to an HVAC partner.
The HVAC partner is introduced to the homeowner through the plumber and pays the plumber an unspecified referral fee.

ideas.delivery: The HVAC partner visits the homeowner to inspect the system and may provide further service; the plumber makes the introduction.
ideas.other_uk_rules: If the plumber shares homeowner contact details with the HVAC provider, UK GDPR requires an appropriate lawful basis and transparent handling.

idea.name: Content media business
idea.one_liner: A media business invests in content and grows an audience; the transcript reports revenue but does not say who pays or how it is monetized.
idea.customer: Audience and paying customer are not stated.
idea.offer: Content and audience development; specific media products are not described.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated. The speaker reports revenue and content spend but does not identify the source of revenue.

key_quotes.quote: Here's what my rocks looked like in my own media business three years running.
So year one, we made over $3 million in revenue on less than $10,000 of content spent.
Year two, we did about five million against 200,000. So that's 25 to one.
Year three, seven million on roughly one million invested in content. So seven to one.
